Mino Space is a private commercial satellite company based in Beijing, China, working in the aerospace and manufacturing sectors according to its Crunchbase profile. The listing shows about $403 million in total funding, most recently in December 2025, which suggests a well-capitalised venture-backed business. Its customers and product range are not clear from the available data, but satellite makers and launch-service firms typically sell to government agencies, telecom operators and data buyers. Not a consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Natural Gas Services Group (NGSG) rents and services natural gas compressors, mainly rotary screw and reciprocating units used in oil and gas production, from Midland, Texas. Customers are oil and gas producers and midstream operators in US shale basins, and revenue comes from monthly rental fees plus compressor sales and aftermarket service. Listed on the NYSE under NGS, with a fleet of several thousand units and revenue in the low hundreds of millions of dollars. B2B industrial company with almost no consumer brand awareness.

OceanFirst Bank is the banking subsidiary of OceanFirst Financial Corp, a regional bank holding company headquartered in Toms River, New Jersey and listed on Nasdaq as OCFC. It offers retail and commercial banking, mortgages, wealth management and ATM and branch services across New Jersey, the Philadelphia area and New York, with roughly $13 billion in assets after acquiring Sun Bancorp in 2018 and Partners Bancorp in 2022. Makes money on lending spreads and fees. Regional consumer brand with local visibility in the US Northeast.

Onyx Renewable Partners is a New York-based developer and owner of distributed clean energy projects in the United States, focused on solar and energy storage for commercial, industrial, utility and community customers. It earns money by developing, financing and selling or operating projects and by selling power under long-term contracts. The Crunchbase profile shows about $439 million of funding raised in 2025, indicating a fast-growing, investor-backed platform. B2B energy developer with little consumer brand awareness.

Otto Candies is a family-owned marine transportation company based in Des Allemands, Louisiana, founded in 1909. It operates offshore support vessels, tugs and barges serving oil and gas, offshore wind and heavy-lift customers, mainly in the US Gulf of Mexico and internationally, and earns revenue from vessel charters and towing contracts. The Crunchbase entry shows about $450 million of financing in late 2025. Privately held B2B maritime firm with strong industry reputation but little public brand awareness.

Oxford Lane Capital is a publicly traded closed-end investment fund, listed on Nasdaq as OXLC, that invests mainly in the equity and junior debt tranches of collateralised loan obligations (CLOs). It is managed by Oxford Lane Management from Greenwich, Connecticut, and is sold to retail and income-seeking investors through its shares and preferred stock. Revenue is investment income distributed as monthly dividends. A financial vehicle with no consumer products and little brand awareness outside the investment community.

Renewi is a waste-to-product company that collects, sorts and recycles commercial and industrial waste, turning it into materials such as recycled plastics, compost, energy and construction products. It serves businesses and municipalities mainly in the Netherlands, Belgium and the UK, with annual revenue of about 1.9 billion euros and roughly 7,000 employees. Formerly listed on the London Stock Exchange (RWI), it was acquired by Macquarie Asset Management in 2025. B2B and municipal services firm with limited consumer brand visibility.

Selective Insurance Group is a US property and casualty insurer, listed on Nasdaq as SIGI and based in Branchville, New Jersey, founded in 1926. It sells commercial lines (business, workers' compensation, commercial auto), personal lines and excess and surplus lines through independent insurance agents across about 30 states, with premiums of roughly $4-5 billion a year. Revenue comes from premiums and investment income. Well known with agents and regional businesses, with modest national consumer awareness.

Seven States Power is an energy company based in Chattanooga, Tennessee, described by Crunchbase as a renewable energy company active in consulting and energy services. The listing shows about $439 million of total funding, with the most recent round in January 2025, suggesting it develops or finances power generation capacity. Its customers are likely power utilities and commercial energy buyers in the southeastern United States, though this is not confirmed. B2B energy business, no clear consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

South Wind Exploration & Production is an energy company based in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, working in oil and natural gas exploration and production according to its Crunchbase industries of energy and natural resources. The listing shows $400 million of total funding, last dated in 2025, which points to a private-equity or institutionally backed upstream operator. Revenue would come from selling produced oil and gas to midstream buyers and refiners. B2B resources company with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

The Liberty Company is a commercial insurance and financial services firm based in Gainesville, Florida, per its Crunchbase profile. The listing shows roughly $440 million in total funding, last dated in 2025, which is large for an insurance brokerage and suggests private-equity backing or an acquisition vehicle. Customers are likely businesses buying commercial coverage, and revenue would come from commissions and fees. B2B services firm with local regional visibility, not a consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Tide is a London-based business banking and financial platform for small and medium-sized businesses, founded in 2015. It offers business current accounts through partner banks, invoicing, accounting integrations, credit and a growing set of admin tools, and also runs in India. It has over a million members and is among the largest SME banking brands in the UK, earning revenue from subscriptions, card interchange, lending and platform fees. Venture and growth-equity backed, valued above $1 billion. Strong SME brand, modest consumer awareness.

Ursa Major is a Colorado-based aerospace and defense propulsion company, founded in 2015 and based in Berthoud, that designs and manufactures rocket engines and solid rocket motors using 3D printing. Products include the Hadley liquid engine and Draper and Lynx-class motors, sold to the US Department of Defense, defense primes, hypersonic programmes and space launch customers. It has raised around $450 million in venture and government-backed funding. Private B2B and government supplier with little public brand awareness.

Vanguard Renewables is a Massachusetts-based developer of renewable natural gas, building anaerobic digesters on dairy farms and food-waste facilities that convert manure and food waste into biogas, electricity and fertiliser. Its Farm Powered programme has partnered with large food and beverage brands, and with utilities such as Dominion Energy, with Brookfield-backed financing. It earns revenue from gas sales, environmental credits and processing fees. Operates mainly in the US; B2B with limited consumer awareness, though it works with brands including Starbucks and Ben & Jerry's.

Vaquero Midstream is a Dallas, Texas energy infrastructure company providing midstream services such as natural gas gathering, processing and water handling, mainly in the Delaware Basin of West Texas and New Mexico. Customers are upstream oil and gas producers who pay fee-based rates under long-term dedications. The Crunchbase entry shows about $400 million in funding, indicating a private-equity-backed platform. B2B energy infrastructure operator with no consumer brand visibility.

Western Alliance Bank is the main subsidiary of Western Alliance Bancorporation (NYSE: WAL), a bank holding company based in Phoenix, Arizona, with more than $70 billion in assets. It serves commercial clients nationwide through specialised national business lines such as homeowner associations, mortgage warehouse lending and technology and innovation banking, with regional retail banking in Arizona, California and Nevada. Revenue comes mainly from net interest income and fees. Well known in business banking and a sponsor of some regional sports events, with modest consumer awareness.

Angel Oak Mortgage Solutions is the lending arm of Angel Oak Companies, an Atlanta, Georgia financial services firm focused on non-qualified mortgages (non-QM) for borrowers such as self-employed people and real estate investors who do not fit standard agency criteria. It originates and sells loans through mortgage brokers and correspondent lenders across the US, and the wider group runs asset management and a listed mortgage REIT (Angel Oak Mortgage REIT, NYSE: AOMR). B2B2C finance brand, low consumer awareness.

Billie is a Berlin-based fintech founded in 2017 that offers Buy Now, Pay Later payments for business customers, letting merchants sell on invoice to other companies while Billie pays the merchant upfront and takes on the credit risk. It serves online shops and B2B marketplaces, mainly in Germany and other European markets, and earns fees on transactions. It has raised over $300 million in equity and debt facilities, with backers including Cathay Innovation and Sequoia-linked investors. B2B fintech with low consumer awareness.

DOOR is a St. Louis, Missouri technology company that Crunchbase describes as providing integrated hardware and software, tagged under apps and artificial intelligence. The listing shows about $342 million in total funding, with the most recent round dated in 2025, indicating substantial investor backing. The customer type and specific product are not clear from the available data, so it should be treated as an early-stage B2B technology business in the US Midwest. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Energy Monster (Guaishou Chongdian) is a Shanghai-based operator of shared power bank rental stations, where users rent portable chargers through an app or mini-programme in restaurants, shopping centres, transport hubs and entertainment venues across China. It earns revenue from rental fees and advertising on devices and screens. Listed on Nasdaq (ticker EM) since 2021 after a SPAC-style IPO, with several hundred thousand points of presence and millions of users. High consumer visibility in China, with little exposure elsewhere.

Forge Global is a San Francisco marketplace for trading shares of private companies, serving accredited investors, employees seeking liquidity, and institutions through its Forge Private Market platform and data products. It earns transaction fees, custody and data subscriptions. It was listed on the NYSE (FRGE) in 2022 through a SPAC merger and in 2025 agreed to be acquired by Charles Schwab. It was founded in 2014. Finance-sector brand known among investors and startup employees, but with little general consumer awareness.

InVision was a New York-based design collaboration platform, founded in 2011, used by product teams to create, share and test digital prototypes, and later Freehand, an online whiteboard. At its peak it served millions of designers and most of the Fortune 500, and it raised about $350 million, reaching a valuation around $2 billion in 2018. It was a remote-first company, and it shut down its main products in December 2024. B2B software brand known in the design community, now defunct.

Koiviston Auto is a Finnish bus operator based in Lahti, one of the country's largest bus companies, running regional, commuter, express and charter coach services, including under Matkahuolto and public transport contracts. Customers are passengers, municipalities and public transport authorities who tender routes, and the company also does tours and rentals. It is a family-controlled business with a large fleet of buses and several hundred employees. Visible locally through bus branding, but a regional services firm rather than a national consumer brand.

Lightricks is a Jerusalem-based software company, founded in 2013, behind consumer creative apps including Facetune, Videoleap, Photoleap and Motionleap, plus LTX Studio and the open-source LTX video model for generative AI video. It earns subscription revenue from hundreds of millions of app downloads and from API and studio products. It has raised over $300 million in funding and is valued above $1 billion. Strong consumer app brand with a global user base, especially among creators and social media users.

Myer is Australia's largest department store group, headquartered in Melbourne (Docklands) and listed on the ASX as MYR. It sells fashion, beauty, homewares and electronics through about 55 large stores and an online store, with over 10 million loyalty programme members. In 2024 it took over Premier Investments' Apparel Brands business, adding Just Jeans, Dotti, Jacqui E, Portmans and Jay Jays. Founded in 1900, it is a household retail name across Australia.

OfferUp is a mobile and online marketplace for buying and selling used goods locally in the United States, based in Bellevue, Washington and founded in 2011. It merged with rival Letgo in 2020, and has expanded into shipping, vehicle sales and business listings. It earns money from promoted listings, transaction fees and ads. It has raised close to $400 million and has tens of millions of monthly users. Consumer brand with strong awareness in the US among classifieds users.

PLAYSTUDIOS develops and operates free-to-play mobile and social casino-style games, including myVEGAS Slots, Pop! Slots, myKONAMI Slots and Tetris-themed titles, with a loyalty programme that lets players redeem points for real-world rewards from partners such as MGM Resorts and Hilton. Customers are mobile gamers worldwide, and revenue comes from in-app purchases and advertising. Listed on Nasdaq (MYPS) since a 2021 SPAC merger. It has a US headquarters in California with large studios in Las Vegas, Israel and Europe. Strong brand among mobile gamers.

Zhangyue Technology (iReader) is a Beijing-based Chinese digital reading company that runs the iReader mobile reading app and the Zhangyue e-reader devices, offering web novels, e-books and audio content to subscribers and ad-supported users. Revenue comes from content payments, subscriptions, advertising and hardware sales. It has raised about $365 million, and was an early mobile reading platform in China, with hundreds of millions of installs. Consumer brand in China, little visibility outside the country.

AGS Airports is the owner and operator of Aberdeen, Glasgow and Southampton airports in the UK, headquartered in Paisley, Scotland. Together the three airports handle over 15 million passengers a year, earning revenue from airline passenger charges, retail, parking and property. It was long owned by Ferrovial and Macquarie-managed funds. Glasgow is the largest, with routes to Europe and North America, while Aberdeen serves the North Sea energy sector. B2B infrastructure operator whose airport brands are well known to UK travellers.

AMTD Digital is a Hong Kong-based company that describes itself as an integrated digital solutions platform, with businesses spanning digital financial services, media (the L'Officiel brand licences), art trading, hospitality and investment. It is part of the AMTD group and listed US ADSs on the NYSE under HKD in 2022, becoming known for an extraordinary share price spike despite small revenue. Customers include corporate and financial clients in Asia. Little consumer awareness except the L'Officiel fashion titles.

Ava Labs is a New York-based blockchain developer, founded in 2018 by Cornell professor Emin Gun Sirer, that created Avalanche, a high-throughput smart-contract platform with its own AVAX token and customisable subnets (L1s) used for DeFi, gaming, tokenised assets and institutional projects. It earns revenue from ecosystem grants, partnerships, token holdings and enterprise projects. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Polychain and others, with about $290 million raised publicly. Well known in crypto, with sports sponsorship history, but little awareness among general consumers.

Bitso is a Mexico City-based cryptocurrency exchange, founded in 2014, and one of the largest in Latin America. It lets consumers and businesses buy, sell and send crypto and stablecoins, with strong remittance flows between the US and Mexico, and operates in Mexico, Argentina, Brazil and Colombia. It makes money from trading spreads and fees, and has millions of users. Backed by Coinbase Ventures, Tiger Global and Paradigm, and a known consumer brand in Mexico, including football sponsorship deals.

CircleCI is a San Francisco-based software company, founded in 2011, that offers a continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) platform used by developers to automatically build, test and deploy code. It sells subscription plans to software teams from startups to large enterprises, in cloud and self-hosted form, and claims a large share of open-source and commercial projects. It has raised around $315 million from investors including Greenspring and Sapphire. B2B developer tool well known among engineers but not to general consumers.

CoinSwitch is a Bangalore-based cryptocurrency platform, founded in 2017, which grew into one of India's largest crypto exchanges and later added stocks and mutual funds. It serves retail investors, with millions of users, earning commissions and fees. Backed by Coinbase Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital India, it raised at a valuation near $1.9 billion in 2021. It ran heavy advertising campaigns in India, including cricket sponsorship and celebrity-led ads, making it a recognised consumer brand.

M1 Holdings runs M1 Finance, a Chicago-based personal finance platform founded in 2015 that combines automated portfolio investing, borrowing, high-yield savings, checking and a rewards credit card in one app. Customers are US retail investors, with several hundred thousand active users and billions of dollars in assets, and revenue comes from lending, interchange, premium subscriptions and payment for order flow. It has raised over $300 million. Known fintech brand in the US, though smaller than the big retail brokerages.

Orion Digital Corp. is a financial technology company based in Vancouver, British Columbia, building apps and financial services products according to Crunchbase. The listing shows about $315 million of funding raised, last dated in 2025. Customers and specific products are not clear from the available data. It appears to be a venture-backed Canadian fintech, but it should be verified before any outreach, as same-sounding names exist. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Vayyar is an Israeli semiconductor and sensor company based in Yehud, near Tel Aviv, founded in 2011, that makes 4D imaging radar chips and sensors. They are used in car interiors (child presence and occupancy detection), smart homes and elder care (fall detection), robotics, security and industrial uses. Customers are automakers, Tier 1 suppliers and device makers, and revenue comes from chips and modules. It has raised about $300 million. Strong B2B technology reputation but little consumer awareness.

Ascona Group Holdings is a company based in Pembroke Dock, Wales, United Kingdom, that Crunchbase describes as offering financial services and commercial activities. The listing shows about 200 million in total funding, but gives few details on its products, customers or ownership. It appears to be a UK-based holding company in finance and commercial services, likely B2B, with no confirmed consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cebu Pacific, operated by Cebu Air Inc. and listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (CEB), is the Philippines' largest low-cost carrier, based in Pasay City and founded in 1988 by the Gokongwei family's JG Summit group. It flies domestic and international routes across Asia, Australia and the Middle East with a fleet of about 90 Airbus aircraft, and carries over 20 million passengers a year. Revenue comes from fares and ancillaries. Very high consumer visibility in the Philippines.

Liquid Global is a Tokyo-based cryptocurrency exchange operator, behind the Liquid and Quoine platforms, which provides trading in Bitcoin, Ethereum and other digital assets for retail and institutional customers, mainly in Japan and Asia. Revenue comes from trading fees. It was acquired by FTX in 2022, and its operations were affected by FTX's later collapse. Funding of around $257 million is listed in Crunchbase. Niche crypto brand with limited consumer awareness.

Mixpanel is a San Francisco product analytics company, founded in 2009, that sells software letting product, marketing and engineering teams track how users behave in apps and websites, including funnels, retention and session replay. Customers include thousands of technology and consumer companies, paying subscription fees based on event volume. It has raised about $277 million from backers including Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital and has several hundred employees. B2B software brand known among product teams, not consumers.

Recharge is a Santa Monica, California software company that provides subscription management and recurring billing for e-commerce merchants, particularly on Shopify, BigCommerce and other platforms. Brands use it to sell subscriptions and memberships and manage customer portals, and it earns software fees plus a share of processed payments. It has raised about $277 million, including a large 2021 round, and powers many thousands of online stores. B2B technology brand with no consumer recognition.

Royal Jordanian Airlines is the flag carrier of Jordan, based in Amman, and founded in 1963 as Alia. It flies from its Queen Alia International Airport hub to over 40 destinations in the Middle East, Europe, Asia and North America. It has been a member of the oneworld alliance since 2007, and carries around 3 million passengers a year with a fleet of Airbus and Embraer aircraft. The Jordanian government remains the majority owner. Strong brand in Jordan and the region and an established sponsor of local events.

SparkPost was a Columbia, Maryland email delivery and analytics company that sold a cloud service helping senders reach inboxes at high volume, used by large brands and software firms such as Zillow and PayPal. It earned usage-based subscription fees. Formed from the Message Systems business and backed by Vista Equity, it was acquired by messaging company MessageBird in 2021, and the combined business was later rebranded Bird. B2B developer and marketing infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Zhangshang Tangyi is a Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China health management platform and mobile app, listed by Crunchbase under health care and mobile apps. The listing shows about $275 million in total funding. It appears to serve patients, probably people with chronic conditions such as diabetes, through digital tools and related health services, though this is not confirmed in the data. Likely a China-focused consumer health app. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Autoroute de Liaison Seine-Sarthe (ALIS) is the concession company that built, operates and maintains the A28 motorway section between Rouen and Alencon in Normandy, France, headquartered near Bosrobert in Eure. It is a toll motorway concession, with revenue from tolls paid by drivers and trucks over a contract of several decades. Funding of about 200 million is listed. Infrastructure operator with a regional road-user profile but no consumer brand.

BinDawood Holding is a Saudi retail group based in Jeddah that operates the BinDawood and Danube hypermarkets and supermarkets, mainly in Makkah, Jeddah, Riyadh and other Saudi cities, as well as online grocery delivery. It sells groceries, fresh food and household goods to consumers, with dozens of stores and many thousands of employees. Listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) since 2020 after an IPO. The family founded the first store in the 1980s. Well known consumer retail brand in Saudi Arabia.

Deliverect is a Ghent, Belgium software company, founded in 2018, whose platform connects online orders from delivery apps such as Uber Eats, Deliveroo and Just Eat, plus own-website ordering and kiosks, directly into restaurant point-of-sale systems. It serves restaurants, food chains and ghost kitchens in over 50 countries, charging subscription fees. It has raised about $237 million and passed unicorn status in 2022. B2B hospitality technology brand, strong among restaurants but unknown to general consumers.

Forrestania Resources is an Australian company based in Subiaco, Western Australia, whose Crunchbase entry lists information technology but which appears to be a small resources and exploration-style business, given its name and location. The listing shows about 344 million Australian dollars in funding, though this figure and the nature of the business should be verified. No product or customer details are available. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Healthcare.com is a Miami, Florida insurtech platform that lets users compare and buy health insurance plans online, according to Crunchbase, where it is tagged under fintech, health care and insurance. The listing shows about $244 million in total funding. Customers are US consumers shopping for health coverage, and revenue is likely commissions from insurance carriers, though this is not confirmed. Consumer-facing brand, but awareness is unclear. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Highland Electric Fleets is a Beverly, Massachusetts company that provides electric school buses and other fleet electrification as a service. It handles vehicles, charging infrastructure, financing, maintenance and energy management for school districts and transit operators, who pay a fixed service fee instead of buying the buses. It operates across the United States and has raised about $225 million in equity and project financing. Founded around 2020, it has become one of the larger US electric school bus providers. B2B and public-sector brand with limited consumer awareness.

Humble Group is a Swedish consumer goods group based in Stockholm that buys and grows small direct-to-consumer and fast-moving consumer brands in categories such as personal care, health and wellness, and home products, selling through retailers and online. It has made many acquisitions across the Nordics and Europe and is listed in Stockholm. Funding of around 2.3 billion Swedish kronor is shown on Crunchbase. A holding group whose individual product brands are more visible than the group name itself, mainly in Nordic retail.

LogicSource is a Westport, Connecticut procurement and sourcing services company that helps enterprises cut indirect spend, such as marketing, facilities and professional services, by combining category expertise with technology and managed sourcing teams. Customers are large corporations, including restaurant and retail operators. It earns fees from managed procurement contracts and has raised about $229 million. B2B services firm with a limited public profile and no consumer brand awareness.

Menlo Micro makes the Ideal Switch, a micro-electromechanical (MEMS) switch that behaves like a mechanical relay but is chip-sized, handling high power and radio frequencies. The Irvine, California company, spun out of General Electric research, sells it to makers of test equipment, communications systems, aerospace and defense gear, and power and industrial devices. It earns revenue from components and has raised around $228 million in venture funding. B2B semiconductor supplier, no consumer brand awareness.

Rain is a Manama, Bahrain digital asset platform, founded around 2017, that offers cryptocurrency trading and custody for retail and institutional customers in the Middle East and North Africa, and holds a Central Bank of Bahrain licence. It earns trading and service fees and is one of the larger regional crypto exchanges, with funding of about $223 million listed. Known among crypto investors in the Gulf, but with little awareness among the wider public.

Suncrete is a Dallas, Texas construction materials business, described by Crunchbase as providing high-quality concrete solutions and tagged under construction and logistics. The listing shows about $226 million in total funding, which suggests private-equity backing and acquisitions of local ready-mix operators. Customers are likely contractors, builders and developers in Texas, and revenue comes from selling and delivering concrete. B2B building materials firm with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Totalplay is a Mexican telecommunications company based in Mexico City and part of Grupo Salinas, owned by Ricardo Salinas Pliego, which sells fibre-to-the-home triple-play packages of broadband internet, pay TV and telephony to households and businesses, with a growing enterprise services unit. It is Mexico's largest fibre provider with millions of connected homes, earning subscription revenue. It issues debt in capital markets, and sells through a strong direct sales force. Well-known consumer telecom brand in Mexico.

Yunzhangfang is a Nanjing, Jiangsu company providing cloud-based finance, accounting and tax management software and services to small and medium-sized businesses in China, with products for bookkeeping, invoicing and tax filing. It earns subscription fees and service income and has raised roughly $244 million from investors. Customers are small Chinese firms and accounting agencies. Mainly a B2B brand in China with little recognition outside the SME software market.

HUboo is a Denver, Colorado company that, according to Crunchbase, provides cross-border freight, warehousing and related logistics services. The listing shows about $270 million in total funding, which is substantial for a logistics start-up, but there are no further details on its customers, scale or ownership. It is most likely a B2B logistics and supply-chain business serving e-commerce sellers and importers. No known consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Ampere is an Indian electric vehicle maker based in Bengaluru, producing electric scooters and three-wheeler load carriers under the Ampere name, sold through a dealer network across India for both consumers and fleet operators. It became part of Greaves Cotton's electric mobility business (Greaves Electric Mobility), which has manufacturing in Tamil Nadu and has raised outside investment of roughly $210 million. A recognisable consumer EV scooter brand in India, with TV and sports advertising.

Binance.US is the American cryptocurrency exchange that licenses technology from Binance, offering retail and institutional users trading in dozens of digital assets, staking and custody in the United States. It launched in 2019 and is operated separately from Binance's global exchange, with a separate US management team and an office in Miami after leaving the earlier Palo Alto base. Revenue comes from trading fees. It faced SEC litigation in 2023, later dropped in 2025. Known among US crypto traders, with moderate wider awareness.

Burger King India is the master franchisee of Burger King in India, run by Restaurant Brands Asia Limited (RBA), based in Mumbai and listed on the NSE and BSE since a 2020 IPO. It operates a few hundred company-owned fast-food restaurants serving burgers, wraps and chicken products, with vegetarian-heavy menus, including dine-in, drive-through and delivery. Revenue is about 2,000-2,500 crore rupees. It also owns the Indonesian Burger King franchise. Well-known consumer brand, with strong awareness in Indian cities.

EPG is a Shanghai, China company that Crunchbase describes as a provider of prefabricated (modular) data centers, tagged under data center and data integration. The listing shows about $200 million in total funding. Customers are likely cloud, internet and enterprise operators building computing capacity in China, and revenue comes from selling and delivering modular facilities. B2B infrastructure supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Genomma Lab Internacional is a Mexican consumer goods company that develops and markets over-the-counter medicines and personal care products across Latin America, the US and Spain, backed by heavy television advertising. Its brands include Asepxia, Cicatricure, Goicoechea, Unesia, Tafirol (in Argentina) and Silka. It sells to pharmacies and supermarkets, has annual revenue near 20 billion pesos, and is listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (LAB.B). Crunchbase shows its Argentine entity; the group is based in Mexico City. Highly visible consumer brands in Latin America.

Global Cellulose Fibers is a Memphis, Tennessee manufacturer of cellulose specialty fibres and pulp, described by Crunchbase as having seven pulp mills and two further sites. The listing shows $200 million in total funding. Customers would be industrial producers of filtration, absorbent hygiene, food casings and other specialty products, and revenue comes from fibre sales. B2B commodity-materials supplier with no consumer brand, though the Memphis location suggests ties to the former Buckeye Technologies business. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Laiye is a Beijing artificial intelligence and automation company, founded in 2015 and previously known for robotic process automation (RPA) and intelligent document processing, now offering AI agents and enterprise workflow tools. It serves large Chinese enterprises in finance, telecoms and manufacturing, plus some international clients, and earns software licence and subscription fees. It has raised about $200 million from investors including Hillhouse and Sequoia China. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

Iyuno (written lyuno in the listing) is a Burbank, California media localisation company providing subtitling, dubbing, accessibility and translation services to studios, streaming platforms and content creators, increasingly using AI tools. Following mergers with SDI Media and other firms, it operates studios in dozens of countries and counts major streamers among its customers. It earns project fees and has raised about $206 million. B2B entertainment supplier with little consumer awareness.

MTN Group Fintech is the financial technology arm of MTN Group (JSE: MTN), the Johannesburg-headquartered mobile network operator. It runs the MoMo mobile money and payments services across Africa, plus digital lending, insurance and remittances for tens of millions of mostly unbanked and underbanked consumers and merchants. It earns transaction fees and interest. Investors, including Mastercard and Sanlam-linked partners, acquired minority stakes in a funding round of about 3.8 billion rand. Parent MTN is a high-profile brand, with MoMo widely used across Africa.

Reputation is a San Ramon, California software company that helps multi-location businesses, including car dealers, healthcare groups, banks and retailers, manage online reviews, listings, surveys and customer experience with analytics and AI tools. Previously known as Reputation.com, it sells subscription software to enterprises and has raised about $210 million. Customers are mainly in the US. B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness.

RoboSense is a lidar sensor maker for advanced driver assistance and autonomous vehicles, founded in Shenzhen, China, with a US office in Plymouth, Michigan. It supplies automotive lidar to carmakers and robotics companies, and has supplied large Chinese brands including BYD, Zeekr, Li Auto and Xiaomi. It listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange in 2024. Crunchbase shows about $212 million raised from investors. B2B supplier to automakers, with moderate awareness in the auto industry and none among consumers.

Skylo is a Mountain View, California company that provides non-terrestrial network connectivity, letting ordinary smartphones, IoT devices and vehicles send messages and emergency alerts via geostationary satellites. It works with mobile carriers and device makers, and is the satellite provider behind the Google Pixel satellite SOS and Samsung Galaxy features, plus Verizon and Deutsche Telekom partnerships. It earns service fees from carriers and manufacturers and has raised over $200 million. Its technology reaches consumers, but the Skylo brand is mostly known to the telecoms industry.

U. K. Financial is a London-based company that Crunchbase describes as having created the Maya Coin for its business, tagged under blockchain and cryptocurrency. The listing shows about $200 million in total funding, though this figure and the nature of the operation are unverified. Customers and products are not clear from the data available, and similar-sounding names exist. Treat as an unproven crypto or digital asset business. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

A1R Water is a Miami, Florida company that Crunchbase tags under commercial and food and beverage, and which describes itself as working at the crossroads of technology and water.
