CMR Surgical is a Cambridge, UK medical robotics company, founded in 2014, that makes the Versius surgical robot, a modular, portable robotic system for minimally invasive keyhole surgery. It sells or leases to hospitals in Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Latin America and the US, and earns revenue from systems, instruments and services. It has raised about $1.7 billion in funding from investors including SoftBank, Tencent and Cambridge Innovation Capital. B2B medical device brand, known to hospitals and surgeons but not consumers.

Concentrix is a customer experience (CX) outsourcing and technology company, headquartered in Newark, California and listed on Nasdaq as CNXC, spun off from Synnex in 2020. It runs contact centers and digital services for large clients in technology, retail, banking, healthcare and telecoms, and merged with Webhelp in 2023. It has around 450,000 employees across more than 70 countries and revenue of about $9-10 billion. B2B service provider with little consumer awareness but significant scale.

Curaleaf is one of the largest cannabis companies in the world and the biggest US multi-state operator, with headquarters listed in New York and a large operating base in Massachusetts, and shares listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange and the TSX (CURA). It grows, makes and sells cannabis flower, vapes, edibles and CBD products through its own dispensaries and wholesale in about 20 US states and in Europe, with revenue near $1.3 billion. Strong cannabis consumer brand, but regulated advertising limits its marketing.

Henry Schein is a Melville, New York distributor of health care products and services, listed on Nasdaq as HSIC, supplying dental practices, physician offices, laboratories and animal health clinics. It sells consumables, equipment, software and practice management services in more than 30 countries, with about 25,000 team members and revenue of around $12 billion. Customers are dentists, doctors and vets. The business was founded in 1932. Well known among dental and medical professionals, but not a consumer brand.

Hydnum Steel is a Spanish start-up planning a flat steel plant in Puertollano, Ciudad Real, that would produce low-carbon steel using green hydrogen and direct reduced iron with electric arc furnace technology. It aims to supply automotive and appliance manufacturers with flat rolled products. Planned investment is around 1.6 billion euros, and it is backed by industrial and infrastructure investors. Currently a project-stage company, a B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand recognition.

Linde is the world's largest industrial gases company, listed on Nasdaq and NYSE (LIN), formed in 2018 from the merger of Linde AG and Praxair. It supplies oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, argon and specialty gases, plus engineering and equipment, to healthcare, chemicals, energy, food, electronics and manufacturing customers in over 100 countries. Revenue is about $33 billion and it has around 65,000 employees. The Crunchbase listing shows the Woking, UK base of its engineering operations. B2B giant with low consumer awareness.

Marvell Technology is a Santa Clara, California fabless semiconductor company, listed on Nasdaq as MRVL, that designs chips for data infrastructure, including custom AI accelerators, electro-optics, Ethernet switching, storage controllers and automotive networking. Its customers are cloud providers such as Amazon, Microsoft and Google, telecom equipment makers and automakers. Revenue is around $6-7 billion. It was founded in 1995. B2B chipmaker widely known in technology and investment circles, with almost no consumer brand awareness.

Mercer Advisors is a Denver, Colorado wealth management firm and one of the largest registered investment advisers in the United States, offering financial planning, investment management, tax and estate services to affluent families and retirees. It has grown by acquiring dozens of independent advisory firms, and manages well over $100 billion in client assets. It is backed by private equity investors and earns advisory fees. Regional and referral-based brand, with modest awareness among the general public.

MMG is a base metals mining company headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, and listed in Hong Kong (HKEX: 1208), majority owned by China Minmetals. It operates copper, zinc, lead and nickel mines including Las Bambas in Peru, Kinsevere in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Dugald River in Australia. Revenue is several billion dollars a year, and it sells concentrates and metal to smelters and traders. B2B commodity producer with little public brand awareness.

Nexans is a French cable and electrification company, based in Courbevoie near Paris and listed on Euronext Paris, that makes power cables for utilities and offshore wind, high-voltage subsea interconnectors, building cables and industrial and automotive cables. It has about 28,000 employees in over 40 countries and revenue of around 6-7 billion euros. Customers are power grid operators, construction firms and manufacturers. Founded in 2000 from Alcatel's cable business. B2B industrial supplier with limited consumer awareness.

Novelis is the world's largest producer of flat-rolled aluminum products and the largest recycler of aluminum, based in Atlanta, Georgia and owned by India's Hindalco Industries. It sells sheet and plate to makers of beverage cans, car bodies and speciality products, with plants across North America, Europe, Asia and South America and revenue of about $16-17 billion. Its main customers include beverage companies and automakers. B2B industrial company with limited consumer brand recognition.

Osaic is a Scottsdale, Arizona wealth management and independent broker-dealer firm, formed from the 2023 rebrand of Advisor Group after combining Ladenburg Thalmann and other businesses. It supports roughly 10,000 financial advisors across many broker-dealer brands, providing technology, compliance, clearing and investment platforms, and serves millions of retail clients. It is owned by private equity firms including Reverence Capital Partners and Stone Point Capital. B2B financial services brand with limited consumer awareness.

Pivot Energy is a Denver, Colorado developer, owner and operator of distributed solar and community solar projects in the United States, developing solar for commercial customers, utilities, municipalities and subscribers. It earns revenue from selling power and energy credits under long-term contracts, and has raised financing totalling about $1.8 billion. It operates in many states, including Colorado, Illinois, Maryland and Minnesota. B2B renewable developer with limited consumer brand awareness.

Praxis Precision Medicines is a Boston-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq as PRAX, developing treatments for central nervous system disorders such as epilepsy and essential tremor. Its drug candidates include ulixacaltamide, vormatrigine and relutrigine, and it relies on genetic insights into neuronal excitability. Pre-revenue, it funds its work through equity offerings, with about $1.7 billion raised in total, and partners with other drug developers. Not a consumer brand, with awareness limited to the biotech and investor communities.

RadNet is a Los Angeles-based provider of outpatient diagnostic imaging, listed on Nasdaq as RDNT, operating hundreds of imaging centers across the US that offer MRI, CT, PET, mammography and ultrasound, plus AI and digital health tools through its DeepHealth division. Patients are referred by physicians, and RadNet earns fees from insurers and health systems. Revenue is about $2 billion. Founded in 1985. Known as a healthcare services provider in the regions where it operates, with moderate local consumer awareness.

Rosebank Industries is a London-based investment holding company, listed on the London Stock Exchange, that was set up in 2021 to acquire and improve mid-sized industrial businesses, and has been led by experienced industry executives. It earns income from its portfolio companies and makes acquisitions, with funding of about 1.9 billion pounds shown in Crunchbase. A listed vehicle for industrial investments, with no consumer brand profile.

Sisecam is a Turkish glass and chemicals group, headquartered in Istanbul, and listed on Borsa Istanbul (SISE), controlled by Turkiye Is Bankasi. It produces flat glass, glassware, glass packaging and soda ash and chemicals, with operations in Turkey, Europe, Russia, Egypt and the US (Wyoming soda ash). Revenue is around $4 billion and it has more than 20,000 employees. Founded in 1935 as Turkiye Sise ve Cam Fabrikalari. Sells consumer glassware brands such as Paşabahçe, giving it good brand visibility in Turkey and Europe.

Sixth Street Lending Partners is a closed-end, externally managed business development company (BDC) sponsored by Sixth Street, the global investment firm, that lends to US middle-market companies through direct loans and then pays investors dividends. It raises capital from wealth management clients and institutions, with about $2.1 billion in funding listed. Crunchbase shows San Francisco; the parent is based in Dallas and San Francisco. A financial vehicle with no consumer brand awareness.

Sphere Entertainment is a New York-based live entertainment and media company, listed on the NYSE (SPHR), spun off from Madison Square Garden Entertainment in 2023. Its main asset is Sphere, the 18,000-seat venue in Las Vegas with a huge LED interior and exterior screen, hosting residencies such as U2 and The Wizard of Oz immersive film, and it also owns MSG Networks, the regional sports channels. Revenue comes from ticketing, sponsorship, advertising and media rights. Very high consumer visibility and a significant sponsorship property.

Squadron Energy is an Australian energy company, based in Sydney, owned by Seven Group Holdings (Kerry Stokes), developing and operating gas-fired power stations, a gas import terminal at Port Kembla, wind and solar farms and battery projects. It sells electricity and gas to the national electricity market and large customers, with funding of about 3.7 billion Australian dollars shown. B2B energy brand, with limited consumer visibility.

SSM Health is a Catholic, not-for-profit health system based in St. Louis, Missouri, operating hospitals, physician practices, urgent care and post-acute care in Missouri, Illinois, Oklahoma and Wisconsin. It employs over 30,000 people and has tens of thousands of physicians and staff, with revenue of about $10 billion, and runs the SSM Health Cardinal Glennon Children's Hospital. Patients and insurers pay for services. Strong regional brand in the Midwest.

TA'ZIZ Methanol is a methanol production company at the TA'ZIZ industrial chemicals hub in Ruwais, Abu Dhabi, backed by ADNOC and international partners, building one of the world's largest low-carbon methanol plants using ADNOC gas. It will sell methanol to chemicals and fuel customers globally, with about $2 billion in funding listed. Project-stage or newly operating industrial company, with no consumer brand visibility.

Troilus Gold is a Toronto-based mining development company, listed on the TSX (TLG), advancing the Troilus gold and copper project in Quebec, Canada, a former producing mine under redevelopment. It is pre-revenue, funding itself through equity raises and project finance, and has completed feasibility studies for an open pit mine. It has raised about 2 billion Canadian dollars in total value, according to Crunchbase. Known to resource investors, but with no consumer brand awareness.

United Ports is a French port and terminals business, based in Marseille, formed through a partnership between shipping giant CMA CGM and the infrastructure investor Stonepeak. It owns and operates container terminals and related port assets, earning handling fees from shipping lines and logistics customers, with about $2.4 billion in funding listed. B2B infrastructure company with limited public brand awareness, though its parent CMA CGM is a major global shipping brand.

Vallourec is a French producer of premium seamless steel tubes and tubular solutions, based in Meudon and listed on Euronext Paris (VK). Its products serve oil and gas, power generation, industrial and construction customers, with plants in Europe, Brazil, the US and Asia, about 15,000 employees and revenue of around 4 billion euros. It restructured heavily in 2021 and has since recovered. B2B industrial supplier with strong industry reputation but little consumer awareness.

Sears Holdings Corporation was the parent of the Sears and Kmart department store chains, created in 2005 when Kmart bought Sears, Roebuck and Co. At its peak it operated thousands of stores in the US, selling appliances, tools, clothing and household goods, and brands such as Craftsman, DieHard and Kenmore. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2018, and most of its assets were bought by Eddie Lampert's ESL Investments in 2019. Historically a hugely recognised American retail brand, now a shell of its former self.

Whop is an online marketplace and platform, founded in 2021, where creators and businesses sell digital products, software, courses, paid communities and memberships, with built-in payments, access control and affiliate tools. It serves creators, traders, online entrepreneurs and small digital businesses, and earns a percentage of transactions. The Crunchbase figure of about $478 million in funding looks high for its venture funding, and may include other measures, and no HQ is shown in the data. Popular among online creators, with limited general consumer awareness.

Alibaba Cloud (Aliyun) is the cloud computing and data intelligence arm of Alibaba Group, headquartered in Hangzhou, China, and the largest cloud provider in China and Asia-Pacific. It sells computing, storage, databases, AI models such as Qwen and security services to enterprises, governments and developers across data centers worldwide. Parent Alibaba is listed on the NYSE (BABA) and the Hong Kong exchange (9988). Alibaba is a worldwide partner of the International Olympic Committee, which makes the group a known sports sponsor. B2B brand.

Avient is an Avon Lake, Ohio specialty polymer materials company, listed on the NYSE (AVNT), formed from PolyOne after it sold its commodity businesses. It makes colorants, additives, engineered materials, composites and sustainable solutions for packaging, consumer goods, healthcare, automotive and building customers worldwide. It has about 9,000 employees and revenue of around $3.2 billion. B2B materials supplier, with low consumer awareness but a strong reputation among product manufacturers.

AZZ Inc. is a Fort Worth, Texas industrial company, listed on the NYSE (AZZ), providing hot-dip galvanizing and coating services for steel, plus aluminium and metal coil coatings, in the US and Canada. It serves construction, infrastructure, transmission, solar and appliance customers, and has sold its former energy and electrical equipment business. Revenue is around $1.5 billion. Founded in 1956. B2B industrial services firm with no consumer brand awareness.

Berry Global is a plastic packaging and engineered products maker based in Evansville, Indiana, formerly listed on the NYSE (BERY), with plants worldwide supplying containers, closures, films, nonwovens and healthcare products to consumer goods, food and industrial customers. It merged with Amcor in a deal completed in 2025 that created a much larger packaging group. Revenue was around $12 billion. B2B supplier whose products are used by well-known brands, with low consumer awareness of the company itself.

Chandra Asri is Indonesia's largest integrated petrochemical company, based in Jakarta and listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (TPIA), producing olefins (ethylene and propylene), polyolefins such as polyethylene and polypropylene, styrene monomer and butadiene at its Cilegon complex in Banten. Customers are plastic, packaging, automotive and consumer goods manufacturers in Indonesia and Asia. It is controlled by the Barito Pacific group and, since 2019, also by Thailand's SCG Chemicals, which holds a stake. B2B commodity chemicals producer, little consumer awareness.

Cliffwater Corporate Lending Fund is a US interval fund based in Marina Del Rey, California, managed by Cliffwater LLC, an alternative investment adviser, that invests primarily in senior secured loans to middle-market US companies and offers retail investors access to private credit. It raises money by selling shares to wealth management clients and distributes income as dividends. Crunchbase shows about $1.4 billion in funding. A financial vehicle with no consumer brand awareness.

DOF is a Norwegian subsea and offshore marine services company, based in Storebo near Bergen, listed on Oslo Børs (DOFG). It owns and operates a fleet of offshore construction and subsea support vessels (CSVs and PSVs) used in the oil and gas and offshore wind industries, and provides subsea engineering, ROV services and project management across the North Sea, Brazil and other regions. Customers are energy majors such as Petrobras and Equinor. B2B maritime services firm with no consumer brand awareness.

Dye & Durham is a Toronto-based provider of legal practice management software and cloud services, listed on the TSX (DND), growing through acquisitions of legal, financial and regulatory software businesses in Canada, the UK, Australia and elsewhere. Its products serve law firms, financial institutions, government agencies and corporates, with recurring subscription revenue. It has faced governance disputes and leadership changes in recent years. B2B software company with little consumer brand awareness.

Eastman Chemical is a Kingsport, Tennessee specialty materials company, listed on the NYSE (EMN), spun off from Eastman Kodak in 1994. It makes advanced materials, additives, fibers and chemicals, including Tritan copolyester used in consumer products and the Naia fibers, and has molecular recycling operations. Customers are packaging, building, automotive, personal care and consumer goods makers, with revenue of about $9 billion and around 14,000 employees. B2B supplier, with brand recognition through products used in consumer goods.

JERA Global Markets is the Singapore-based international trading arm of JERA, Japan's largest power generation company, formed in 2015 by Tokyo Electric Power and Chubu Electric Power. It trades LNG, coal, power and carbon products and manages fuel procurement for JERA, with offices in Singapore, London and the US. Funding of about $1.5 billion is shown in Crunchbase. B2B energy trading firm with little public brand awareness.

Koppers is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania integrated global provider of treated wood products and wood treatment chemicals, and carbon compounds, listed on the NYSE (KOP). Products include railroad ties, utility poles, residential lumber and chemicals, carbon pitch used in aluminum production and other industrial chemicals. Customers are railroads, utilities, lumber retailers and industrial users in North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, with revenue of around $2 billion. B2B industrial brand with limited consumer awareness.

Monotype is a Woburn, Massachusetts typography and design company, long known for Helvetica, Arial and other fonts, and owner of the MyFonts, Fonts.com and Linotype libraries, which license fonts to brands, device makers and software developers. It also provides brand design services. It was a listed company, then taken private by HGGC in 2019 for about $825 million. Customers include Apple, Microsoft and major consumer brands. B2B design supplier, with high recognition in the design community but low consumer awareness.

Nordson is a Westlake, Ohio precision technology company, listed on Nasdaq (NDSN), making dispensing, coating, fluid control and testing equipment, as well as medical and electronics inspection systems. Customers are manufacturers of packaging, consumer goods, medical devices and electronics, in more than 35 countries, with revenue of about $2.7 billion and roughly 8,000 employees. Founded in 1954. B2B industrial equipment brand with no consumer awareness.

NortonLifeLock was the consumer cyber safety company behind Norton antivirus, LifeLock identity theft protection and later Avast, AVG and Avira, headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. It was renamed Gen Digital in 2022 after merging with Avast, and is listed on Nasdaq (GEN). It sells subscriptions to hundreds of millions of consumers, with revenue of about $4 billion. Norton is one of the best-known consumer security brands worldwide.

Parkland is a Calgary, Alberta fuel distributor and convenience store operator, listed on the TSX (PKI), with retail brands including Chevron, Ultramar, Pioneer and On the Run in Canada, plus fuel supply operations in the US and the Caribbean and the Burnaby refinery. It serves consumers, commercial fleets and industrial customers. Revenue is about 30 billion Canadian dollars. In 2025 it agreed to be acquired by Sunoco LP. Its retail fuel stations have high consumer visibility across Canada.

Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) is the flag carrier of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, based in Solna near Stockholm, and a member of the SkyTeam alliance. It flies to over 100 destinations from hubs in Copenhagen, Oslo and Stockholm, carrying about 25-30 million passengers a year. It restructured through Chapter 11 in the US in 2022-2024, and in 2025 Air France-KLM agreed to take a majority stake. Strong consumer brand in Scandinavia and a sponsor of sporting and cultural events.

Slack is the San Francisco workplace messaging and collaboration platform, founded in 2013 out of the game company Tiny Speck, used by companies and teams for channels, direct messages, calls, workflows and app integrations. It listed in 2019 and was acquired by Salesforce in 2021 for about $27.7 billion, and now operates as part of Salesforce with AI features. It has tens of millions of daily users. Very well known in business and technology, but mostly a B2B brand.

Trinseo is a Wayne, Pennsylvania specialty materials company, listed on the NYSE (TSE), formerly part of Dow's styrenics business (Styron) until its sale in 2010 and the rename in 2015. It makes plastics, latex binders, synthetic rubber and engineered materials for automotive, packaging, consumer goods, building and paper customers, with plants in Europe, the US and Asia. Revenue is around $3.5 billion. B2B materials supplier with low consumer awareness.

Valmet is a Finnish developer and supplier of technologies, automation and services for pulp, paper, board and energy industries, headquartered in Espoo and listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (VALMT), spun off from Metso in 2013. It serves mills and energy producers worldwide, selling process equipment, automation systems and service contracts, with about 19,000 employees and revenue of around 5 billion euros. B2B industrial brand with strong reputation in its sector and no consumer awareness.

ADNOC Drilling is the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's drilling arm, listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADNOCDRILL) and based in Abu Dhabi, operating one of the largest fleets of onshore and offshore drilling rigs in the Middle East, and providing integrated drilling services including directional drilling and fluids. Its main customer is ADNOC, and it earns day-rate and service revenue. It expanded into the US through the Enersol joint venture. B2B oilfield services firm with no consumer brand.

Allegro MicroSystems is a Manchester, New Hampshire semiconductor company, listed on Nasdaq (ALGM) and majority owned by Japan's Sanken Electric, that makes magnetic sensors and power ICs used in electric vehicles, ADAS, industrial automation and data centers. Customers are automakers and industrial manufacturers, with revenue of about $700-1,000 million. It has operations in the US, Philippines and Thailand. Established in 1936 as part of Sprague Electric. B2B chip supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Blackstone Secured Lending Fund (BXSL) is a New York business development company listed on the NYSE, managed by Blackstone, that lends to US middle-market companies through first-lien senior secured loans. It is one of the largest listed BDCs with a portfolio near $10-12 billion in assets, and it pays regular dividends to shareholders. It raises capital from investors rather than selling products. Financial vehicle that benefits from Blackstone's name but has no consumer brand awareness of its own.

Constellation Software is a Toronto-based acquirer and operator of vertical market software businesses, listed on the TSX (CSU), founded by Mark Leonard in 1995. Through operating groups such as Volaris, Harris, Jonas, Vela and Perseus, it buys and runs hundreds of small software companies serving public transport, healthcare, hospitality, utilities and government. Revenue is over $10 billion. B2B holding company, well known in investment circles, with little public brand awareness.

Douzone Bizon is a Seoul-based South Korean business software company, listed on KOSDAQ, offering ERP, accounting, tax, groupware and cloud-based services for small and mid-sized businesses and large enterprises, including the Amaranth and iCUBE products. It earns subscription and licence revenue, with funding of about 1.4 trillion Korean won shown in Crunchbase. B2B software brand in South Korea, with little recognition outside the country.

Fabbrica Italiana Sintetici (FIS) is an Italian pharmaceutical chemicals manufacturer, based in Montecchio Maggiore near Vicenza in Veneto, founded in 1957, that makes active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), intermediates and custom synthesis for generic and branded drug companies worldwide. It is a major supplier of APIs for cardiovascular, anti-inflammatory and other medicines, with production sites in Italy and about 1,000 employees. It has been owned by private equity investors. B2B ingredient supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

KeHE Distributors is a Naperville, Illinois wholesale distributor of natural, organic, specialty and gourmet food, and wellness products, serving independent natural stores, supermarket chains and e-commerce retailers across the United States and Canada. It carries tens of thousands of products from emerging and established brands, and earns distribution margins and fees. A family-held business founded in 1952 with about 6,000 employees and revenue of around $7-8 billion. B2B supplier, known in the natural foods industry but not to shoppers.

Kraton is a producer of styrenic block copolymers and pine-based specialty chemicals, headquartered in Houston, Texas, with a historical base in The Woodlands, and plants in the US, Europe and Brazil. Its products are used in adhesives, tyres, coatings, personal care, roads and consumer goods. It was previously listed on the NYSE (KRA) and was acquired by DL Chemical in 2022 for about $2.5 billion. B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

LegalZoom is an online legal services and business formation company, founded in 2001, that helps consumers and small businesses create LLCs and corporations, wills, trademarks and other legal documents, and offers attorney advice, compliance and tax services. It is listed on Nasdaq (LZ) and has served millions of customers in the US and the UK. Revenue is about $700 million, from subscriptions and one-off services. Crunchbase lists a Mountain View address. Widely known consumer and small business brand in the US, backed by heavy advertising.

LivingSocial was a Washington, D.C. online daily deals marketplace, founded in 2007, that offered discounts on local restaurants, activities and travel, competing with Groupon, and was backed by Amazon, which invested about $175 million. It grew rapidly to dozens of countries, but then shrank as the daily deals model declined. It was acquired by Groupon in 2016. Once a recognisable consumer brand in the US and abroad, it is now defunct as a standalone business.

Localiza is Brazil's largest car rental company, headquartered in Belo Horizonte, listed on the B3 exchange in Sao Paulo (RENT3), and one of the largest in Latin America. It rents cars to consumers and companies, runs long-term fleet outsourcing and the Seminovos used car retail business, and merged with rival Unidas in 2022, creating a fleet of more than 600,000 vehicles. Founded in 1973. Strong consumer brand in Brazil with a heavy retail presence, plus Localiza Meoo and Hertz franchise operations.

Magnite is the largest independent sell-side advertising platform, listed on Nasdaq (MGNI), formed from the combination of Rubicon Project and Telaria with later acquisitions of SpotX and SpringServe. Its technology lets publishers, streaming TV services and app owners sell ad inventory automatically to agencies and brands, and it earns a share of ad spend. Revenue is about $600-700 million. Based in Los Angeles, with offices in New York and other cities. B2B advertising technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Malaysia Airlines is Malaysia's flag carrier, based at Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Sepang, Selangor, and part of Malaysia Aviation Group. It is a member of the oneworld alliance and flies to about 60 destinations across Asia, Europe, Australia and the Middle East. It is owned by the government through Khazanah Nasional, after being restructured following the 2014 flight disappearances, and carries around 15-20 million passengers a year. Strong national consumer brand and a visible sponsor of sporting and cultural events in Malaysia.

New Mountain Finance Corporation is a business development company (BDC), listed on Nasdaq (NMFC) and managed by an affiliate of New Mountain Capital, that lends to US middle-market companies in defensive growth sectors such as software, healthcare and business services. It holds a portfolio of about $3 billion and pays a quarterly dividend. Crunchbase shows a Denver address; the sponsor is based in New York. A financial investment vehicle with no consumer brand awareness.

Ocorian is a fund administration, corporate services and private client services business, headquartered in the Channel Islands and London, which supports private equity funds, real estate funds, corporates and wealthy families with administration, trust, accounting and fiduciary services across about 25 jurisdictions. It was formed from the rebrand of Estera and other firms, and is owned by private investors. Crunchbase lists about 800 million in funding. B2B professional services firm with low public brand awareness.

Outokumpu is a Finnish stainless steel producer, headquartered in Helsinki and listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (OUT1V), with mills in Finland, Sweden, Germany, the UK and the US (Alabama). It produces stainless steel sheets, plates and long products for construction, transport, appliances, food processing and chemicals customers, and recycles scrap. It has about 8,000 employees and revenue of about 6-7 billion euros. B2B industrial company with little consumer visibility.

PTC is a Boston-area industrial software company, listed on Nasdaq (PTC), founded in 1985, whose products include Creo CAD, Windchill product lifecycle management, ThingWorx for industrial IoT, Onshape cloud CAD and Vuforia augmented reality. Customers are manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, medical devices and industrial equipment, who pay subscription fees. Revenue is about $2.5 billion. B2B software brand, widely known among engineers and manufacturers but not among consumers.

QI-ANXIN (Qi An Xin) is a Beijing-based cybersecurity company, founded in 2014 by the former 360 executive Qi Xiangdong, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market (688561). It sells network security products, threat intelligence, endpoint and data security, and managed security services to government agencies, state-owned enterprises and large companies in China. Revenue is several billion yuan. B2B security brand with a strong profile in China among enterprise and government buyers, and no consumer presence.

Royole is a Shenzhen-based maker of flexible displays and sensors, founded in 2012, best known for the FlexPai, the first commercially sold foldable smartphone (2018). It also sold flexible OLED screens, smart wearables, and the Moon cinema headset. It raised about $1 billion at a valuation near $5 billion, but later ran into financial difficulties and restructuring. Some brand awareness in tech press and electronics trade fairs, but with limited commercial scale today.

SK Siltron CSS is the silicon carbide (SiC) wafer business of South Korea's SK Siltron, based in Bay City, Michigan, which it acquired from DuPont in 2020. It makes SiC substrates and epitaxial wafers used in electric vehicle power electronics, chargers and renewable energy inverters, supported by a US government CHIPS Act grant and Department of Energy loan. Customers are power chip manufacturers. Part of the SK Group. B2B semiconductor materials supplier with no consumer awareness.

Spiber is a Japanese biotechnology company based in Tsuruoka, Yamagata, founded in 2007, that uses microbial fermentation to produce Brewed Protein, a structural protein material for fashion, outdoor apparel and other applications. It has partnered with The North Face and Goldwin on Moon Parka and other products, and has raised about $976 million. It earns revenue from material sales and licensing. B2B materials developer, but known among fashion and outdoor brands.

The Exchange, formally the Army and Air Force Exchange Service (AAFES), is a Dallas, Texas-based US Department of Defense retail organisation, with a history over 125 years, that runs stores, restaurants, gas stations, e-commerce and services for active-duty military personnel, retirees and their families on bases worldwide. It sells everyday goods tax-free, and its profits support morale, welfare and recreation programmes. It has more than 20,000 employees and revenue of about $7-8 billion. Strong brand within the US military community.

TiVo is the San Jose, California digital video recorder pioneer, founded in 1999, whose set-top boxes let viewers record and pause live TV, and which later became a platform and licensing business for pay-TV providers. It merged with Rovi in 2016 and with Xperi in 2020, and the intellectual property business was later spun out as Adeia in 2022. Its consumer TiVo brand and software are now sold via cable operators and TV makers. Historically a household name among US early adopters.

Ayvens is a Rueil-Malmaison, France-based vehicle leasing and fleet management company, formed in 2023 by the merger of ALD Automotive and LeasePlan, and majority owned by Societe Generale. It leases and manages roughly 3 million vehicles in over 40 countries for corporate fleets, SMEs and individuals, and also offers flexible subscription services and used car sales. Listed on Euronext Paris (AYV). Revenue and its fleet size are among the largest in the world. B2B-led brand with growing consumer subscription visibility.

Boom Supersonic is an Englewood, Colorado aerospace company, founded in 2014, developing Overture, a planned supersonic passenger aircraft with orders and options from airlines such as United, American Airlines and Japan Airlines, and the XB-1 demonstrator which made supersonic flights in 2025. It is also developing its own Symphony engine and a power turbine for data centers. It has raised about $730 million in funding, and has faced a long certification timeline. Well-known aviation brand in the media, with strong public interest.

BRC Group Holdings is a Los Angeles-based diversified provider of financial and business services, according to Crunchbase, which tags it under business development. The listing shows about $735 million in total funding. Details of its subsidiaries, customers and ownership are not provided in the available data, and the name is similar to BRC Inc., the Black Rifle Coffee company, so it should not be confused with it. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Brevo, formerly Sendinblue, is a cloud-based digital marketing platform headquartered in Paris, offering email and SMS marketing, marketing automation, CRM, live chat and transactional messaging for small and medium businesses. It has hundreds of thousands of customers worldwide on subscription plans, and has raised about $780 million in funding including a 2021 round led by Bridgepoint. Founded in 2012. B2B software brand with growing marketing profile but little consumer awareness.

BuzzFeed is a New York digital media company, listed on Nasdaq (BZFD), known for viral lists, quizzes, news (BuzzFeed News closed in 2023), and food and lifestyle brands such as Tasty, plus HuffPost and Complex acquisitions. It earns money from advertising, commerce and content licensing, with revenue of a few hundred million dollars. Founded in 2006 and listed via a SPAC in 2021. Large online audience, particularly among younger readers, and a high-profile consumer media brand.

Carbon is a Redwood City, California 3D printing company, founded in 2013 as Carbon3D, whose Digital Light Synthesis technology and printers produce production-quality polymer parts for manufacturers. Customers include Adidas (4D running shoe midsoles), dental labs, automotive and medical device companies, which buy printers on subscription plus resins. It has raised about $740 million and was valued at $2.5 billion in 2018. B2B industrial technology brand, known in manufacturing but less so with consumers.

Carpenter Technology is a Philadelphia-area producer of specialty alloys and stainless steels, listed on the NYSE (CRS), headquartered in Wyomissing and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. It makes titanium, nickel and cobalt alloys, powder metals and additive manufacturing products for aerospace, defense, medical, transportation and energy customers. Revenue is about $2.5 billion and it has been in business since 1889. B2B metals producer with a strong industry reputation but little consumer awareness.

Cascades is a Quebec-based manufacturer of tissue, containerboard and packaging products, headquartered in Kingsey Falls and listed on the TSX (CAS), founded in 1964. It produces recycled-fibre paperboard, corrugated packaging and tissue and hygiene products for consumers and the away-from-home market in Canada and the US. It has about 10,000 employees and revenue of roughly 4.5 billion Canadian dollars. Regional consumer and B2B brand, with Cascades Pro and branded tissue lines.

CloudWalk Technology is a Chinese artificial intelligence company focused on facial recognition and computer vision, founded in 2015 in Guangzhou and now with headquarters listed in Shanghai, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. It sells face recognition systems for finance, public security, airport and transport customers, plus smart city platforms, and counts Chinese government and bank clients. It has raised about 5.6 billion yuan. B2B and government supplier, with low consumer awareness and some regulatory scrutiny.

Doma was a San Francisco-based real estate title and escrow insurer that applied machine learning to speed up title insurance for home purchases and refinances, selling through lenders, real estate agents and consumers. It listed on the NYSE (DOMA) through a SPAC in 2021 and was acquired in 2024 by Title Resources Group. Funding of roughly $680 million is listed. B2B2C insurance brand with limited consumer awareness.

Etsy is a Brooklyn, New York online marketplace, founded in 2005 and listed on Nasdaq (ETSY), where independent sellers sell handmade, vintage and craft goods. It also owns Reverb, Depop and Elo7, and earns revenue from listing and transaction fees, advertising and seller services. It has more than 90 million active buyers, with gross merchandise sales of around $13 billion. Strong consumer brand in the US, UK and Europe, with extensive marketing.

Fang Holdings (formerly SouFun) is a Beijing-based Chinese real estate internet portal, listed in the US as ADS, providing property listings, new home sales, rental, home furnishing and online financing services in China. It earns revenue from listing fees, advertising and commissions, and was once one of the largest property websites in China. It has raised about $706 million in total and has shrunk in recent years. Known as a property site in China, with little recognition outside.

foodpanda is an online food and grocery delivery marketplace owned by Delivery Hero of Berlin, with a regional base in Singapore, operating across Asia, including Pakistan, Bangladesh, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. It connects consumers with restaurants and shops through an app and earns commissions, delivery fees and ad revenue. Founded in 2012 by Rocket Internet. It exited several Asian markets, including Taiwan, which Uber agreed to buy in 2024 but was blocked. Strong consumer brand in Asia.

Ganji.com was a Beijing-based Chinese classifieds website, founded in 2005, where users listed jobs, housing, used goods, cars and services, competing with 58.com. It raised about $710 million, and merged with 58.com in 2015, forming the 58 Group. The Ganji brand then operated as part of 58.com. At its peak, a major consumer classifieds brand in China.

Genco Shipping & Trading is a New York-based owner of dry bulk cargo ships, listed on the NYSE (GNK), operating a fleet of about 40-45 Handysize to Capesize vessels that carry iron ore, coal, grain and steel for commodity traders and miners. It earns revenue from charters and spot freight, and emerged from Chapter 11 in 2014. It has about $700 million in total funding listed. B2B shipping company with little consumer awareness.

International Breweries Plc is a Nigerian brewer, based in Lagos with its main plant in Sapele, controlled by AB InBev after it took over SABMiller's Nigerian business, and listed on the Nigerian Exchange (INTBREW). It brews and sells Trophy, Hero, Budweiser, Castle Lite, Grand Malt and Beta Malt, with a large distribution network. Revenue is hundreds of billions of Nigerian naira. Strong consumer beer brands in Nigeria, with extensive sports and entertainment marketing.

JCET Group (Jiangsu Changjiang Electronics Technology) is a Jiangyin, Jiangsu-based semiconductor packaging and testing company, listed on the Shanghai exchange (600584), and one of the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) providers. It serves chip designers in communications, consumer, automotive and computing markets, and acquired Singapore-based STATS ChipPAC in 2015. Revenue is around 35 billion yuan. B2B chip supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

JOLED was a Tokyo-based Japanese maker of printed OLED displays, formed in 2015 from the OLED display businesses of Sony and Panasonic and backed by the government-linked fund JIC and Japan Display. It made medium-sized OLED panels for medical monitors, gaming and professional displays, using inkjet printing. It filed for bankruptcy in 2023 and its assets were sold to Innolux. B2B component supplier with limited consumer awareness.

Le.com (LeTV, Letv) was a Beijing-based Chinese online video and entertainment company, the flagship of the LeEco group founded by Jia Yueting, that offered streaming video, smart TVs, phones and e-commerce. It was listed in Shenzhen as Leshi Internet Information and Technology, and faced a major financial crisis from 2016, with LeEco's collapse. Funding of about 6 billion yuan is shown. Once a high-profile consumer technology brand in China, now a shadow of its former self.

Maire Tecnimont, now operating as Maire, is an Italian engineering and technology group based in Milan, listed on Borsa Italiana (MAIRE). Through NextChem and Tecnimont, it designs and builds plants for fertilisers, polymers, gas processing, hydrogen and chemicals recycling worldwide, working for energy and industrial clients, with revenue of around 5-6 billion euros. B2B engineering contractor with strong industry reputation and no consumer awareness.

Meitu is a Xiamen, China-based consumer app company, founded in 2008 and listed in Hong Kong (HKEX: 1357), best known for the Meitu Xiu Xiu and BeautyCam photo-editing apps, and the Wink video editor and Meitu Design Studio. It earns subscription revenue from hundreds of millions of monthly users, plus advertising and cross-border sales of former Meitu smartphones, and holds large crypto and digital asset reserves. Strong consumer app brand in China and parts of Asia.

National Health Investors (NHI) is a Murfreesboro, Tennessee real estate investment trust, listed on the NYSE (NHI), that owns senior housing communities and skilled nursing facilities, leasing them to operators and lending on healthcare properties across the US. It earns rent and interest income, with a portfolio of about $3 billion. Founded in 1991. A financial and property business with no consumer brand awareness.

Odfjell Drilling is an international offshore drilling and well services contractor, listed on Oslo Børs (ODL) and operating from Aberdeen and Bergen. It owns and operates semi-submersible rigs and drillships, including Deepsea rigs, and provides engineering and platform drilling services for oil majors, mainly in the North Sea, Norway and other regions. Revenue is around $1.1 billion. Related to the Odfjell family business. B2B energy services company with no consumer brand awareness.

Olive was a Columbus, Ohio healthcare automation company, founded in 2012, that sold AI-driven software to automate administrative tasks such as billing, claims and prior authorisation for hospitals. It reached a valuation of over $4 billion in 2021 and raised about $856 million, but it struggled and shut down in 2023, selling parts of its business. B2B healthcare technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Paytm Mall was the e-commerce marketplace of Paytm (One97 Communications), launched in 2017 and backed by Alibaba, Ant Financial and SoftBank, selling electronics, fashion and home goods through the Paytm app and website. Based in Noida, with Crunchbase showing a Bangalore address. It lost large sums competing with Amazon India and Flipkart and was scaled back. It once had good consumer visibility in India.

Postmates was a San Francisco on-demand delivery platform, founded in 2011, that delivered food, groceries and goods from local restaurants and stores via an app, using gig couriers. It raised about $780 million and was acquired by Uber in 2020 for $2.65 billion, and then merged into Uber Eats. It was a recognisable consumer brand in major US cities.

RigUp was an Austin, Texas online marketplace and workforce platform for the energy industry, founded in 2014, connecting oil and gas companies with vetted contractors, service providers and workers. It raised about $750 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Founders Fund and was valued at about $2 billion. It rebranded as Workrise in 2021. B2B workforce brand, known in energy and trades, not to consumers.

Signa Retail was the retail arm of the Signa Group of Austrian investor Rene Benko, based in Vienna, which owned and invested in department stores and retail businesses such as Galeria Karstadt Kaufhof in Germany, KaDeWe Group, Selfridges and online sports retailers. The Signa empire collapsed in 2023, with Signa Holding and Signa Prime entering insolvency, so the Signa Retail business was restructured and its assets sold off. Defunct as a group, though its department store brands retain high consumer visibility in Germany.

Suning Smart Life is a Nanjing, China-based retail business that is part of the Suning group, including the Suning Xiaodian convenience stores and offline smart retail, selling consumer goods, food and beverages through franchised neighbourhood stores and digital services. Crunchbase shows about $750 million in funding. The Suning name is well known in China for the Suning.com consumer electronics chain, and the group owned Inter Milan football club until 2024. Strong domestic brand, but the specific unit is less known.

Syniverse is a Tampa, Florida telecommunications technology company, founded in 1987 (as GTE TSI), providing messaging, roaming, number portability, analytics and network services that connect mobile operators and enterprises. Customers include most of the world's carriers and large businesses, and it is owned by private equity investor Carlyle. It has raised about $780 million. B2B telecom infrastructure company with no consumer brand awareness.

Sysdig is a San Francisco cloud security company, founded in 2013, whose platform secures containers, Kubernetes and cloud workloads through runtime detection, vulnerability management and cloud security posture tools. Customers are large enterprises and technology companies, paying subscription fees. It created the open-source Falco project and has raised about $730 million, reaching a valuation of $2.5 billion. B2B security brand known to developers and security teams, but not to the public.

Taboola is a New York-based content discovery and native advertising company, listed on Nasdaq (TBLA), founded in 2007 in Israel, that recommends articles and videos at the bottom of publisher sites such as news outlets and, through its Realize platform, helps advertisers reach audiences. It earns a share of advertising spend and has revenue of about $1.7 billion, and works with thousands of publishers including Yahoo and NBC News. B2B ad technology brand, with limited consumer awareness.

Telecom Egypt is Egypt's incumbent fixed-line telecommunications operator, headquartered in Giza and listed on the Egyptian Exchange (ETEL), about 80 percent owned by the Egyptian government. It provides fixed voice and broadband under the WE brand, owns a stake in Vodafone Egypt, and is a major international carrier with submarine cable landings and data centers. Customers include households, businesses and other carriers, with revenue of tens of billions of Egyptian pounds. Well known consumer telecom brand in Egypt.

The E.W. Scripps Company is a Cincinnati, Ohio media company, listed on Nasdaq (SSP), that owns about 60 local television stations in over 40 US markets, the ION national broadcast network, and the Scripps News and Court TV brands. It earns revenue from advertising, retransmission fees and network distribution. Founded in 1878 by Edward W. Scripps, it has about 5,000 employees and revenue of around $2.5 billion. Broad national reach through its stations and ION, but a B2B corporate name with low consumer recognition.

Topshop and Topman are UK fashion retail brands formerly owned by Arcadia Group (Sir Philip Green), which collapsed into administration in 2020. Their brands and online business were bought by ASOS in 2021 for about 265 million pounds, with Nordstrom taking a minority stake, and are now sold via ASOS and partner retailers rather than the previous high street chain. Topshop was a household name for women's fashion in the UK, with a global following, and the brand has been relaunched online.

Wolt is a Helsinki-based food and retail delivery platform, founded in 2014, that lets consumers order from restaurants, shops and supermarkets in about 25 countries across Europe, Israel and Asia, delivered by courier partners. It earns commissions and delivery fees. It was acquired by DoorDash in 2022 in a deal worth about $8.1 billion, and still operates under the Wolt brand. Strong consumer app brand in the Nordics, Central Europe and Japan.

Yidao Yongche (Yongche) is a Beijing-based Chinese ride-hailing and car service company, founded in 2010, that offered premium chauffeured rides through an app, competing with Didi and Uber China. It raised about $790 million from investors, including LeEco, and later faced losses and restructuring. It was one of the early luxury car-hailing brands in China. Consumer recognition is limited compared with Didi, and it is less prominent today.

Aalberts is a Dutch industrial technology group, based in Utrecht and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (AALB), with businesses in building technology, industrial and semiconductor technology. It makes piping systems, valves, surface treatments and precision parts, selling to installers, wholesalers and manufacturers in over 50 countries. It has about 15,000 employees and revenue of around 3 billion euros, and was founded in 1975. B2B industrial brand with strong trade recognition but little consumer awareness.

Access TeleCare is a Dallas, Texas telemedicine company, founded in 2008, that provides hospitals with 24/7 telehealth specialist services such as neurology, stroke, psychiatry, critical care and infectious disease, delivered by video from its physician network. Customers are hospitals and health systems across the US, which pay service fees. It has raised about $630 million, including from private equity backers. B2B healthcare provider brand with no consumer awareness.

Aligned Energy, better known as Aligned Data Centers, is a Plano, Texas developer and operator of large-scale wholesale data center campuses, offering high-density, air-cooled and liquid-cooled capacity to hyperscale cloud providers, AI companies and enterprises. It has campuses in the US, Latin America and elsewhere, and in 2025 was agreed to be acquired by an investor group, including BlackRock, GIP, MGX and Microsoft, for about $40 billion. B2B infrastructure brand with little public recognition.

Bitpanda is a Vienna-based investment platform, founded in 2014, where retail customers buy and sell crypto assets, stocks, ETFs, metals and commodities, and which also offers white-label investment services (Bitpanda Technology Solutions) to banks and brokers. It has more than 6 million users in Europe, earns trading fees and spreads, and has raised about $550 million, with a valuation of $4.1 billion in 2021. It is one of Europe's best-known crypto brands.

Blue Yonder, formerly JDA Software, is a Scottsdale, Arizona supply chain software company providing AI-driven planning, demand forecasting, warehouse, transportation and retail planning tools to manufacturers, retailers and logistics companies. It was acquired by Panasonic in 2021 for about $7.1 billion, and itself acquired One Network Enterprises in 2024. It has thousands of customers worldwide and earns subscription and services revenue. B2B software brand, widely known to supply chain professionals, but not to consumers.

C2FO is a Kansas City, Missouri-based working capital platform, founded in 2008, that lets suppliers of large buyers choose to be paid early in exchange for a discount, and gives buyers a way to deploy cash. Customers include large corporates and their suppliers in over 100 countries, and it earns transaction and service fees. It has raised about $570 million from investors including Mastercard, Citi Ventures and Tiger Global. B2B fintech brand known to finance teams but not to consumers.

Canadian Utilities is a Calgary, Alberta energy infrastructure company, listed on the TSX (CU), and a subsidiary of ATCO Ltd. It operates regulated electricity transmission and distribution and natural gas distribution in Alberta, plus natural gas pipelines, energy storage and power generation, serving about 1.5 million customers, with revenue of around 4-5 billion Canadian dollars. Part of the Southern family group. Regulated utility with local consumer visibility in Alberta and the ATCO brand.

Cockroach Labs is a New York company, founded in 2015, that develops CockroachDB, a distributed SQL database designed to survive failures and scale across regions, sold as a managed cloud service and self-hosted software. Customers are enterprises in financial services, retail, gaming and technology, with subscription revenue. It has raised about $633 million and reached a valuation of $2 billion in 2021. B2B database brand known to developers, not consumers.

Comscore is a Reston, Virginia media measurement and analytics company, listed on Nasdaq (SCOR), providing audience measurement, cross-platform viewership data and advertising effectiveness measurement for TV, digital and streaming. Customers are advertisers, agencies, publishers and broadcasters, who buy data and subscriptions. Founded in 1999. It has had a recapitalisation and has shrunk in size since 2018. B2B data brand, known in advertising and media, with no consumer recognition.

Cvent is a Tysons, Virginia event management software company, founded in 1999, whose platform helps organisers plan and market meetings, conferences and hotel sourcing, including event registration, venues and attendee apps. Customers are corporates, associations and hotels worldwide. Previously listed on the NYSE, it was acquired by Blackstone in 2023 for about $4.6 billion. B2B software brand, strong in events and hospitality sectors, with no consumer recognition.

Despegar is the leading online travel agency in Latin America, headquartered in Buenos Aires, Argentina and founded in 1999. It sells flights, hotels, packages and car rentals through the Despegar and Decolar brands in about 20 countries, with revenue from commissions and package margins. It was listed on the NYSE (DESP) and was agreed to be acquired by Prosus in 2024-2025 for about $1.7 billion. Strong consumer brand in Latin America; heavily advertised.

Emicool is a Dubai, United Arab Emirates district cooling company, which provides chilled water services to buildings, developments and government entities across the UAE from central cooling plants. Customers are real estate developers, commercial buildings and government clients, who pay connection and capacity fees plus consumption charges. About 2.25 billion dirhams in funding is shown. B2B utility-type infrastructure provider with little consumer brand visibility.

HighTower Advisors is a Chicago-based wealth management platform, founded in 2007, that supports independent financial advisors with technology, back office, custody access and investment services. It serves high-net-worth clients through hundreds of advisors, with over $100 billion in assets. Backed by private equity including Thomas H. Lee Partners, and it has raised about $645 million. Earns advisory and platform fees. Known among advisors and wealthy families, with limited mass consumer awareness.

Huagong Tech (HGTECH) is a Wuhan, China laser and optoelectronics company, listed on the Shenzhen exchange (000988), that makes laser processing equipment, sensors, optical communication modules and infrared products. It sells to manufacturers in automotive, electronics, energy and industrial sectors, and to telecom equipment makers. It was spun out of Huazhong University of Science and Technology and has revenue in the range of 10 billion yuan. B2B industrial technology supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Illumio is a Sunnyvale, California cybersecurity company, founded in 2013, whose zero-trust segmentation platform prevents breaches from spreading by controlling traffic between workloads, data centers and clouds. Customers are large enterprises, banks, healthcare and government agencies, paying subscription fees. It has raised about $560 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst and was valued at $2.75 billion. B2B security brand, known to IT teams, not consumers.

Irving Pulp & Paper is a Saint John, New Brunswick pulp and paper mill, part of the family-owned J.D. Irving group, which operates a highly integrated forest products value chain from forests and sawmills to pulp, paper and tissue in Atlantic Canada. It sells to publishers, packaging and consumer product makers, with about 660 million dollars in funding listed. Private B2B manufacturer with regional visibility in the Maritimes, while the wider Irving name is well known in Canada.

Jet.com was a Hoboken, New Jersey online retailer, founded in 2014 by Marc Lore, that offered members low prices through a pricing algorithm and warehouse bundling. It raised about $570 million and was acquired by Walmart in 2016 for about $3.3 billion, and was then wound down in 2020. A one-time high-profile e-commerce challenger to Amazon, now defunct as a brand.

KK Group is a company based in Jakarta, Indonesia, described by Crunchbase as providing an online-to-offline imported products retail service. The listing shows about $629 million in total funding. Similar-sounding names exist, including KK Group, a Chinese retail group that runs the KKV stores, and it is unclear which entity this is, so details on products and customers should be verified before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Krafton is a Seoul-based South Korean video game publisher, listed on the Korea Exchange, best known for PUBG: Battlegrounds and PUBG Mobile, which together have hundreds of millions of players, plus inZOI, Subnautica developer Unknown Worlds and other studios. It earns revenue from in-game purchases and game sales, with revenue of around 2.5-3 trillion Korean won. Founded in 2007 as Bluehole. Strong consumer brand among gamers and active in esports and sports sponsorship.

Lucid Software is a South Jordan, Utah visual collaboration company, founded in 2010, whose products include the Lucidchart diagramming tool, Lucidspark whiteboard and Lucidscale cloud visualisation. It sells subscriptions to individuals and enterprises, with tens of millions of users and customers including many Fortune 500 companies. It has raised about $670 million and was valued at $3 billion in 2021. Known in business and education, but mostly a B2B software brand.

Moncler is an Italian luxury fashion house, headquartered in Milan and listed on Borsa Italiana (MONC), famous for its quilted down jackets. Under chairman and CEO Remo Ruffini, it sells ready-to-wear, accessories and outerwear through Moncler and Stone Island, which it bought in 2021, via its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale. Revenue is around 3 billion euros. Founded in 1952 in Monestier-de-Clermont, France. Highly visible luxury consumer brand worldwide.

MTN Nigeria is the Nigerian arm of the MTN Group, based in Lagos and listed on the Nigerian Exchange (MTNN), and the country's largest mobile network operator with over 80 million subscribers. It provides voice, data, mobile money (MoMo PSB), digital and enterprise services. Revenue is in the trillions of naira. Part of Johannesburg-listed MTN. Very high consumer brand awareness in Nigeria, with many sponsorships including football and entertainment.

Noom is a New York digital health company, founded in 2008, offering a subscription weight management and behaviour-change app based on psychology, with coaching, food logging and, more recently, GLP-1 medication programmes. It has had tens of millions of users and raised about $660 million at a valuation of $3.7 billion in 2021. Customers are consumers who pay subscriptions. Strong direct-to-consumer brand in the US, with heavy digital and TV advertising.

Olin Corporation is a Clayton, Missouri manufacturer of chlor alkali products and epoxy, and of Winchester ammunition. Its Chlor Alkali division makes chlorine and caustic soda, Epoxy makes resins, and Winchester produces ammunition for hunters, sport shooters, law enforcement and the military. It is listed on the NYSE (OLN), with revenue of around $6.5 billion. Founded in 1892. Winchester has high consumer visibility among shooters, while the rest of the company is a B2B chemicals supplier.

OppFi is a Chicago-based financial technology platform, listed on the NYSE (OPFI), that uses AI to offer short-term and installment loans, mainly to non-prime US consumers who have limited access to bank credit, through partner banks. It earns interest and fees, with revenue of about $500 million. Founded in 2012 and listed via a SPAC in 2021. Known in the subprime lending and fintech sectors, and a consumer-facing brand promoted by performance marketing.

Orca Security is a cloud security company, founded in 2019 in Israel and now headquartered in Portland, Oregon, whose agentless SideScanning technology scans cloud workloads, configurations and identities for risk across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. It sells subscriptions to enterprises, raised about $630 million, and was valued at $1.8 billion in 2021. B2B cybersecurity brand known to security teams, but not to the general public.

Perimeter Solutions is a Clayton, Missouri specialty chemicals company, listed on the NYSE (PRM), best known for long-term fire retardants for wildfires (Fire-Trol, Phos-Chek) used by US and international forestry agencies, and for firefighting foams and other chemicals. It earns revenue from government and industrial customers, and was formed from the 2021 acquisition of Solvay's phosphorous pentasulfide business and fire retardant businesses. B2B and government supplier with low consumer awareness.

Signet Jewelers is the world's largest diamond jewellery retailer, listed on the NYSE (SIG), with US roots in Akron, Ohio and a legal base in Bermuda. It operates about 2,600 stores under Kay Jewelers, Zales, Jared, Piercing Pagoda, Banter and the online retailer Blue Nile, with revenue of about $6-7 billion. Customers are consumers buying engagement rings, wedding and gift jewellery. Highly recognised in US consumer advertising.

StarPower Semiconductor is a Jiaxing, Zhejiang power semiconductor company, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market (603290), that makes IGBT power modules and chips for electric vehicles, industrial control, solar and wind power, and home appliances. Customers include Chinese automakers and industrial manufacturers. Founded in 2005 and one of China's leading IGBT module suppliers, with revenue of about 3 billion yuan. B2B component maker with no consumer brand awareness.

Studio City Macau is an integrated resort on the Cotai Strip in Macau, owned by Studio City International Holdings (NYSE: MSC), a subsidiary of Melco Resorts & Entertainment. It combines a casino, hotels, the Batman Dark Flight and Golden Reel Ferris wheel attractions, retail, a water park, dining and entertainment venues, aimed at Chinese and Asian leisure visitors. It earns revenue from gaming and non-gaming sources. High-profile destination brand in Macau and Asia, with big events and concerts.

PingCAP, maker of the TiDB distributed database, is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California and was founded in 2015 in Beijing. Its open-source, MySQL-compatible TiDB database handles transactions and analytics at large scale, and is available as the TiDB Cloud managed service. Customers include fintech, e-commerce and gaming companies. It has raised about $640 million. B2B database brand known to developers, with no consumer awareness.

Truphone is a mobile connectivity company, founded in 2006 in London, that provides global mobile services, eSIMs and IoT connectivity platforms for consumers, businesses and device makers. It developed eSIM software and a global network of roaming agreements, aiming to let customers connect without physical SIM cards. Crunchbase lists a base in Amsterdam and funding of about $620 million. B2B connectivity provider with modest consumer awareness.

Twilio is a San Francisco cloud communications company, listed on the NYSE (TWLO), founded in 2008, whose APIs let developers build messaging, voice, video and email features into apps. It also owns Segment (customer data) and SendGrid (email), and serves hundreds of thousands of customers, from startups to large enterprises. Revenue is around $4.5 billion, earned on usage-based and subscription fees. Widely known in technology and developer communities, but a B2B brand with little consumer recognition.

Bank of Cyprus is the largest bank in Cyprus, with headquarters in Strovolos, Nicosia, and shares listed on the Cyprus and Athens exchanges (BOCY). It provides retail, SME and corporate banking, insurance and wealth management, with around 100 branches and about 2.4 million customers. Founded in 1899. Following Cyprus' 2013 bank crisis, it was restructured and is now stable. Very well-known consumer bank in Cyprus.

AM Best is a US credit rating and information agency specialising in the insurance industry, headquartered in Oldwick, New Jersey and founded in 1899. It assigns financial strength ratings to insurers and reinsurers worldwide, publishes industry research and data, and earns fees from rating services and subscriptions. Customers are insurance companies, brokers and regulators. B2B financial information brand, important in insurance, but unknown to consumers.

Acorns is an Irvine, California personal finance and investing app, founded in 2012, that rounds up everyday purchases and invests the change in diversified ETF portfolios, and offers retirement accounts, banking, a debit card and Acorns Early for children. It has several million paying customers and has raised about $513 million. It earns subscription fees of a few dollars a month. A well-known consumer fintech brand in the US, with extensive advertising and partnerships.

Ashtrom Renewable Energy is an Israeli renewable energy developer, based in Tel Aviv, part of the Ashtrom Group, that develops, builds and operates solar and wind power plants in Israel and abroad, including in Eastern Europe and the US, selling electricity under long-term contracts. It is listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Crunchbase lists about $470 million in funding. B2B energy producer with limited consumer brand awareness.

ASML is a Dutch semiconductor equipment company, based in Veldhoven, listed on Euronext Amsterdam and Nasdaq (ASML), and the sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines used to make the most advanced microchips. Customers are chipmakers including TSMC, Samsung and Intel, who pay hundreds of millions of euros per machine. It has about 44,000 employees and revenue of around 28-30 billion euros. Founded in 1984 as a Philips joint venture. Hugely important B2B company with little consumer brand recognition.

Capital Clean Energy Carriers Corp. is a Greek shipping company, headquartered in Piraeus and listed on Nasdaq (CCEC), formerly Capital Product Partners, that owns and operates LNG carriers and other vessels, chartered to energy majors on long-term contracts. It is part of the Marinakis group and is controlled by Evangelos Marinakis. Revenue comes from charter hire. B2B shipping company, with a profile in the sports world through Marinakis' ownership of Olympiacos and Nottingham Forest.

CarDekho is an Indian automotive marketplace group, founded in 2008 in Jaipur and now with offices in Gurugram, that runs CarDekho, Gaadi, ZigWheels, BikeDekho, InsuranceDekho and RupeeDekho. It offers new and used car listings, reviews, financing and insurance, and has hundreds of millions of visits. It earns advertising, lead generation fees and commissions, has raised about $490 million, and is valued above $1.2 billion. Strong digital consumer brand for car buyers in India, with large marketing campaigns.

CarNext.com is a digital used car platform based in Amsterdam, created by LeasePlan (now part of Ayvens), that sells nearly new used cars, many from lease fleets, to consumers online in several European countries with delivery and warranty. It earns revenue from vehicle sales and finance. Founded in 2016 or so, with funding of about 400 million listed. Part of a large leasing group, and a European online car retail brand with modest consumer awareness.

Chargebee is a subscription billing and revenue management software company, founded in 2011 in Chennai, India, and now with its headquarters in the US. Its platform helps SaaS and subscription businesses handle recurring billing, invoicing, payments and revenue recognition. Customers include thousands of businesses such as Freshworks and Calendly. It has raised about $470 million and was valued at $3.5 billion in 2022. B2B fintech software brand with no consumer recognition.

Clari is a Sunnyvale, California revenue operations platform, founded in 2012, using AI to forecast sales, track deals and manage pipeline for revenue teams. Customers are mid-size and large companies such as Okta, Workday and Zoom, which pay subscription fees. It has raised about $500 million, including a 2022 round at a $2.6 billion valuation. B2B software brand known to sales leaders, not to consumers.

Deliverr was a San Francisco e-commerce fulfilment company, founded in 2017, offering fast two-day shipping for online sellers by storing their products in a network of warehouses. It raised about $490 million and was acquired by Shopify in 2022 for about $2.1 billion, then sold to Flexport in 2023 as Shopify refocused. Customers were merchants selling on Walmart, Amazon and Shopify. B2B logistics brand, now folded into Flexport.

Devo is a Boston/Cambridge, Massachusetts cloud-native security analytics company (SIEM and security operations platform), formerly called Logtrust, that ingests and analyses large volumes of machine data for security teams.
